summary: Repaired and applied the SQLite v1→v2 migration on node1. The catalog is healthy and remains correct after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Made upgrade.py transactional and repeat-safe under Python 2.5/SQLite 3.4.2.
Added price_cents as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with insert/update enforcement preventing negative values.
Ensured schema_version changes to 2 only after schema validation succeeds.
Preserved product IDs and descriptions; initialized existing prices to zero.
Verified forced-failure rollback leaves an intact, writable v1 database.
Saved pre-repair script and database backups.
Restarted node1 and verified persistence, integrity, constraints, OS release, and kernel.

evidence.requirement: Transactional migration and correct version sequencing
evidence.summary: Source audit shows BEGIN, schema changes, validation, version update, COMMIT, and exception ROLLBACK ordering; first and repeated live executions succeeded.
Forced failure returned nonzero and left version 1, original columns and rows, no partial constraint triggers, integrity OK, and a successful v1 write test.

evidence.requirement: Retain IDs/descriptions and add zero-initialized nonnegative price_cents
evidence.summary: Live database shows products (1, Paper, 0) and (2, Tape, 0), schema version 2, the new column, constraint triggers, rejected negative input, and integrity OK.

evidence.requirement: Legacy platform compatibility without OS/kernel replacement
evidence.summary: Migration compiles with installed Python 2.5; Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained unchanged through the work and restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID fe2bf43a-03cd-4d8d-baa5-8c6dc5b46546; restart was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to c96860af-67f2-48fb-8351-873d219c3433; post-restart repeat migration, data, constraints, and integrity all passed.
